blocks.text: The opening

**These are Tilde fobs: coins and tags for your keys, with an NFC sticker inside.** Tap one with a phone and it opens whatever’s on the sticker: a link, your contact card, your Wi-Fi. The tags have a QR code too. The box holds a few; here’s every shape, color and icon.
How it works

items.text: **Tap it.** Any phone with NFC reads the sticker inside, and the other person doesn’t need an app.
**Change it any time.** A phone rewrites the sticker through the plastic, so the same fob can open something new without a reprint. You only open it to replace the sticker.
**Scan a tag.** A tag’s QR code opens a short link (up to 53 characters, such as a website). The code is printed, so it doesn’t change. A coin has no code: it’s for tapping only.
**You print it yourself** on a multi-color printer, in two pieces with no pause. Or pick up a tag at the Tilde booth at Web Summit.

Colors
The Tilde booth has three color sets, each two colors, made with the model’s color options. In these three, the code takes the body’s color, with no patch of another color.

items.text: **Khaki on black:** the booth’s giveaway tags

blocks.text: In the model, a tag’s code sits on a light field unless you choose otherwise (**QR Background**).
each fob type in each color set
**Special:** orange fobs, with black icons and the code black on white.
The model’s Theme menu has the cards’ themes (Dark, Light, Signal, USA, Brasil, Portugal and Retro), not these three sets. Or pick your own colors.
the orange fobs
The storage box

A 2 × 2 box of flat stacks: 3 premium coins, 3 premium tags, 5 base coins and 8 base tags, under a sliding lid with the wordmark engraved. It was made for the Tilde booth. Its print files aren’t published.
the storage box, closed and open
Icons
**Tell a set apart** with an icon on the back, and a short label if you like, in a color you choose. Every icon is generic: no brand logos, so a chat bubble rather than any app’s logo.
one image per built icon, with its name from the model and its line from `icon-uses.json`
How to get one

items.text: **Print your own** from [github.com/tbutman/tilde-card](https://github.com/tbutman/tilde-card): choose a coin or a tag, Base or Premium, your colors and your icon in OpenSCAD’s Customizer, then export it.

**Add a round NFC sticker** (an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker””) and write it with Tilde (Android: Cards → Write a sticker) or the free NFC Tools app (iPhone and Android).
**Or pick one up at the Tilde booth at Web Summit.** Take a tag from the giveaway boxes; it’s written for you there (see the Uses page).
